Subject: DPA execution and incident notification timing (FinTechCo)

Jordan —

Thanks for the call earlier. We attached our proposed DPA redlines (FinTechCo_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf) for Redwood to review. Two items we need to lock down before we can execute:

1) Incident first-notice timing: FinTechCo requires "first notice" for any incident impacting customer data within 24 hours of discovery. We call this out in section 5(b). Please confirm Redwood can commit to 24-hour initial notification and a follow-up report timeline (we typically ask for a full incident report within 72 hours).

2) Subprocessors: we need guaranteed notification of new subprocessors at least 14 days before engagement and a current list of subprocessors and locations.

Also: what is your preferred e-sign flow? We use DocuSign — happy to receive an envelope or you can upload to our portal.

Att: FinTechCo_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

Laura — thanks and appreciate the clear ask. High level answers below and next steps.

1) 24-hour initial notice: we can accept an initial notice obligation within 24 hours for confirmed or reasonably suspected security incidents that affect FinTechCo customer data. We prefer the contract language to say: "24-hour initial notice of a suspected or confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data, with a commercially reasonable follow-up timeline (72 hours) for a substantive incident report and remediation plan." That keeps scope tied to security incidents and avoids operational noise.

2) Subprocessors: we can commit to notifying of new subprocessors 14 days in advance for changes that materially affect data processing location or function; we'll provide a current subprocessor list as an attachment.

E-sign: we will prepare the redline bundle and send via DocuSign. Target: send envelope today (Sat) so your team can review first thing Monday. Please confirm the signatory (name/title) and the billing contact for the Master Services Agreement.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20270515.pdf (pdf) — redline highlights include the 24/72 phrasing, limited scope for 24h, and a subprocessor notification clause tweak.

If that all sounds OK I will route to Rishi for legal sign-off and then send DocuSign envelope to the address you prefer.

Cheers,

Marissa / Jordan / Laura —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Legal has reviewed the proposed redlines. A couple of final points before I approve the e-sign flow:

1) Incident language: we will accept the 24-hour initial notice but want the contract to make clear it applies to "security incidents affecting Customer Data," and that Redwood's initial notice will include the detection timestamp, a short summary of impact, and any immediate mitigation steps. We will commit to a more detailed incident report within 72 hours for incidents with confirmed data exposure; if forensic timelines extend, we will provide rolling updates.

Suggested contract sentence: "Provider will notify Customer without undue delay and, in any event, within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery of an incident materially affecting Customer Data; a substantive incident report will be provided within seventy-two (72) hours when reasonably available, with subsequent updates as investigations continue."

2) Subprocessors: accept 14-day notification for new subprocessors that alter the data processing footprint; continue to publish an up-to-date list on a shared drive.

3) Execution: please include the following in the DocuSign envelope: (a) the redline DPA file (DPA_final_for_esign.pdf), (b) DocuSign signing order with Redwood legal (rishi.malhotra@redwood.com) as second signer, and (c) an audit-log acknowledgement page (we will keep a signed copy in our records).

Jordan — go ahead and send the DocuSign envelope to legal@fintechco.com and cc: secops@acme-cloud.com for visibility. Confirm the envelope link in this thread once sent.

— Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
